workItems.title: Deliver trusted Core caller and capability integration with explicit host stages

workItems.title: Settle exact newly owned Windows TLS key containers after native drain
workItems.acceptanceCriteria: Under approved W01, after actual handler/server/body drain and successful owned certificate disposal, settle only the exact newly owned recorded software user-key container if native delete-on-close left its backing. Verify provider/container/unique identity before native deletion and exact absence before Removed custody and slot release. Preserve unknown backend, failed disposal, mismatched identity and cleanup faults as unresolved closed scope; never enumerate stores or key directories, access existing credentials, provision trust, force GC or suppress cleanup failure. Preserve completed WORK-002 history.
workItems.validation: Keep the actual expired RSA TLS negative unchanged and reproduce its successful cleanup through the native certificate suite. Add a retained-key native regression for exact owned deletion and rerun existing custody failure/reentry rows and successful TLS probe against the corrected helper. Include focused build, formatting, independent source review, custody journal and restoration/history documentation. No new backend pool or additional resource ceiling.

workItems.title: Recover required Entra availability independently of business readiness
workItems.acceptanceCriteria: Correct the reviewed required outbound Entra readiness deadlock using the existing Heartbeat owner and reused SDK credential. A temporary startup acquisition failure or idle last-token expiry can recover without a business endpoint or host restart. An observed token timestamp does not alone establish replacement acquisition failure. Keep all caching/mint decisions with the SDK; no force refresh, new cache, scheduler or business-call replay. Coalesce and join admitted recovery/acquisition work, bound repeated probe frequency and diagnostics, and preserve native deadline/cancellation and original faults.
workItems.validation: Add actual facade readiness regressions for recovery after temporary initial acquisition failure and idle expiry without restarting the host; verify business 503 and no effect while genuinely unavailable, later successful acquisition and 200/effect after recovery. Verify explicit source recheck, concurrent/coalesced probes, cutoff/drain and optional/inbound-only behavior with existing public/native seams. Include focused native adapter regressions, scoped build/format, guide/contract review and preserved failure/resource evidence. Real AKS remains unverified. No push, merge or release.

workItems.title: Propagate certificate retirement faults and define Windows chain support
workItems.acceptanceCriteria: Observe eligible retired-generation cleanup before reporting certificate adoption; preserve nonblocking retirement when actual response holds remain. Surface the original cleanup fault and reflect permanent native admission closure in profile status/readiness even on unchanged source material or later body cleanup. Retain the bounded current/draining ownership model. State the Windows leaf-only client transmission arrangements and unsupported root-only peer case explicitly in public guides; no automatic certificate-store writes or existing-key/store inventory, and no unverifiable peer-availability promise.
workItems.validation: Use finite privately journaled W01 fault scopes to test immediate A-to-B Removed callback failure and later held-body retirement failure, original fault propagation, rejected healthy adoption, unchanged-source behavior and status/readiness versus future calls. Add a real intermediate-issued client TLS case: explicit-issuer peer succeeds; isolated root-only peer fails on Windows while Linux supplied-chain behavior is checked if a suitable existing runtime is available. Include focused native REST/certificate regressions, exact owned cleanup audit, scoped formatting/build and current consumer guides. Preserve all completed-owner history, shared limits and external AKS/cert-manager gaps; no tooling/install campaign, push, merge or release.
